title: Columnar Oak: Ancient Fastigiate Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: Quercus robur 'Fastigiata' grows narrow and upright, not spreading. Krakow's lone crossroads oak is put at 140 to 210 years.
intro: Bred to stay narrow instead of spreading, the columnar or fastigiate form of the pedunculate oak grows in a tight upright column that reads as a poplar until you look at the leaf. Nurseries have propagated Quercus robur 'Fastigiata' since the nineteenth century for that shape, which is why it usually turns up in pairs flanking a gate rather than standing alone. Krakow protected the oldest in 2008, a lone tree at a crossroads whose 288-centimetre girth puts its age at roughly 140 to 210 years, calculated rather than recorded. Warsaw has two matched pairs: one flanking the university botanical garden's observatory entrance, designated in 2024, the other on ul. Lowicka, protected in 2013 and visible from the street. Nobody has dated the Warsaw pairs; fastigiate oaks spread through European gardens over two centuries, which rules out a single planting year.
